test_title: SSC CGL Tier 2 English Previous Paper 2 (Held On: 3 Feb 2022)
subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate option to improve the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to improve it, select ‘No improvement required’.

The report, that markets __are open,__ is not true.
solution:
The correct answer is **No improvement is required.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As the subject of the clause is **markets **which is a **plural**, the verb should be in plural form(**are**).
 
• Hence, the sentence is correct.
 
• The correct answer is** option 3.**
 
• We can think that markets are open is wrong because of the rule of "are should be followed by past participle"
 
• But here the word open is not in passive voice.
 
• Here There is a news (report) which is saying that markets are open.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__**

__
 
• Such as Class is open
 
• Class is closed
 
• In the same way here the report which said that the markets are open is not true.
 
• The report is antecedent and **that markets are open** is a dependent clause.
 
• So The use of is according to the Subject the Report is correct.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Relative Pronouns**

 
 
• **​**A relative pronoun is a word that introduces a dependent (or relative) clause and connects it to an independent clause. A clause beginning with a relative pronoun is poised to answer questions such as Which one? How many? or What kind? Who, whom, what, which, and that are all relative pronouns.
 
• Who: Refers to a person (as the verb’s subject)
 
• Whom: Refers to a person (as the verb’s object)
 
• Which: Refers to an animal or thing
 
• What: Refers to a nonliving thing
 
• That: Refers to a person, animal, or thing
